quotes.text: PrimeKG and HPO annotations supply disease–phenotype associations

rationale: Sources (PrimeKG, HPO annotations, public case reports) are named with citations, but no version, snapshot date or per-task route to a source record is given on S1-S3. Task ids in S4 hint at source families but S4 does not count as reporting.

quotes.text: Clinicians select a target disease and associated findings, then construct the presentation from which the agent must infer the diagnosis.

rationale: Origin (clinician-authored from PrimeKG/HPO and case reports, LLM-assisted) and the collection/authoring method are documented. No data licence or terms and no consent/IRB statement or explicit 'not required'; the README Apache-2.0 licence covers code, SkyRL and Qwen3 only.

quotes.text: The corpus contains 304 distinct target-diagnosis labels: 278 occur in one task, 24 occur in two tasks

rationale: Descriptive corpus statistics (disease distribution, 17 subcategories, per-task requirement counts) are reported. No comparison against a named target patient or disease population.

searched: S1 (no unsafe-output or bias test; only dialogue-quality ratings and robustness checks), S2 (research-use-only disclaimer, not a test), S3 (no chunks), S4, S5 (no chunks). Neither an unsafe-output test nor a bias test is reported.

quotes.text: 42 of the 50 held-out diagnoses never occur in training.

rationale: A held-out split and a diagnosis-overlap count exist, but they serve training evaluation, not benchmark contamination control. The tasks and splits are public and there is no gating, canary or pretraining-overlap check; scored as an indirect empirical check (borderline against 2).

quotes.text: The patient persona and scoring key remain inaccessible to the agent.
It could therefore read the answer key in `/var/lib/caa`.

rationale: The paper states isolation of persona and scoring key without naming a mechanism. The README names only an unprivileged agent for current-Harbor evaluation and itself discloses that under the SkyRL-pinned Harbor 0.1.44 the agent runs as root and could read the answer key (disclosed weakness, G5).

quotes.text: Tool execution reads the fixed cache without generating findings online.
The patient simulator (inside each task container) and the must-ask judge (in the verifier) call an LLM.

rationale: Task data and tool findings are fixed cached entries and the training stack is lockfile-pinned. The patient simulator and judge are live LLM API calls identified only by model name (GPT-5.4-mini, Claude Opus 4.6) with no snapshot ids.

quotes.text: Clinicians then inspect live patient–agent simulations and revise inconsistent responses, inappropriate disclosure, or infeasible requirements.

rationale: Manual clinician simulation review of feasibility and agent-based evidence (1,249 frontier trajectories passing all gates over 187 training tasks) support solvability. No scripted reference solution is run through the grader.

searched: S1 (Section 2.2, Appendix B), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5 (no chunks). Tasks do change simulated state (orders, prescriptions, referrals), so NA does not apply. The grader checks required tools, argument-level action constraints and the diagnosis; no check of unchanged or out-of-scope state is reported.

quotes.text: Strict pass@1 requires all gates and all must-ask topics.

rationale: The conjunction of four gates is a stated design argument that makes trivial success unlikely. No empirical random or trivial-agent rate or explicit chance rate is reported; the base Qwen3-4B 0% strict pass@1 is not a trivial-agent baseline.

searched: S1 (Tables 2, 7, 10), S2 (held-out table), S3 (no chunks), S4, S5 (no chunks). No do-nothing or random agent score is reported; the zero-shot Qwen3-4B row is a real model, not a trivial agent.

quotes.text: Re-scoring fixed trajectories with different must-ask judges broadly preserves clinician-model rankings

rationale: The must-ask LLM judge is stress-tested by substitution (Table 9) but never validated against labelled outcomes or human labels with agreement or error figures. The deterministic diagnosis, tool and action gates carry no tests or reference-solution evidence; the clinician study validates patient realism, not the evaluator.

quotes.text: Patient simulation uses temperature 0.7 and history judging uses temperature 0.

rationale: Judge temperature 0 and one rollout per model-task pair are stated, but patient simulation is stochastic at 0.7 with no seed and no repeated-run policy for the headline scores. The safeguards cover only part of the harness.

quotes.text: Paired-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals describe uncertainty in the change in strict pass@1 , measured in percentage points.

rationale: Paired-bootstrap CIs are given for step-cap and SFT/RL comparisons. The headline 31-model comparison (Table 2, Table 7) has no CI or test, although rankings and 'best' are claimed.

quotes.text: Within the Harbor evaluation, each model receives the same tasks and tool interface, with one rollout per model–task pair.
Medium reasoning effort is used across all models.

rationale: Run count (one rollout per pair) and decoding controls (medium reasoning effort, simulator and judge temperatures) are stated. Independence of runs is not stated.

quotes.text: SFT improves over the base model by 8 points, with an interval from 2 to 15 points.

rationale: CIs and SE bars appear for the Qwen3-4B strict pass@1 and held-out accuracy, but the 31-model leaderboard has none. The resampling unit is not explicitly named beyond 'paired-bootstrap', and clustering of tasks within templates or sources is not addressed.
Table 9 reports an original and a repeat condition with differing scores (score-level variation across reruns). No action-level or state-level agreement and no pass^k-type metric is reported.

quotes.text: Medium reasoning effort is used across all models.
Patient simulation uses temperature 0.7 and history judging uses temperature 0.

rationale: Decoding controls including reasoning effort are given. Models are identified by versioned names only, with no provider snapshot id or release date. The harness (Harbor, Terminus-2) has no version or commit stated as matching the reported numbers; the README pins Harbor 0.1.44 only for training, a dependency pin.

quotes.text: The agent discovers tools through clinic tools , which returns their names, descriptions, and JSON parameter schemas.
Write tools update the simulated encounter
A requested laboratory result that is absent may return not_available

rationale: JSON parameter schemas are returned for tools, Table 5 and Appendix B.2 separate read from write behaviour per tool group, and return semantics (not_available, defaults, mocked results, rejected calls) are documented. S5 has no chunks, so whether the read/write distinction reaches the agent-visible tool descriptions cannot be told.

quotes.text: A local dispatch audit of the findings-enabled corpus covered all 3,550 exposed task–tool pairs
The drug-interaction tool returns a mock database response.

rationale: A dispatch audit covers handler behaviour and simulated or mocked behaviour (mock drug-interaction database, defaults, not_available) is disclosed in the appendix. No evidence in the packet that this disclosure reaches the agent-visible surface (S5 empty), so element (iii) is not shown.

quotes.text: These actions do not trigger external clinical services.
Write tools update the simulated encounter

rationale: Write actions (orders, prescriptions, referrals, admissions, plans, diagnosis recording) are identified and stated as simulated records without external services. No scoring or penalty of unsafe or unnecessary writes is reported beyond argument-level action constraints; S5 reach cannot be told.

quotes.text: The resulting dialogue and tool trace are passed to the verifier.
Distinguishing these failures requires explicit assessment of the questions asked and actions taken throughout the encounter.

rationale: Grader input (transcript and tool trace, plus an LLM judge for must-ask topics) is named and the need for process-level assessment is argued. No validation of the grader on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates is reported.

quotes.text: They are authored offline by an LLM and checked for explicit diagnosis leakage before packaging.
The patient persona and scoring key remain inaccessible to the agent.

rationale: Leakage controls exist for tool findings and the scoring key, though the README admits the key is readable in the SkyRL training setup. The held-out split is public (task-id lists in the repo, tasks on Harbor Hub), and no canary or provenance marker is reported.

searched: S1 (Sections 2.3, 4, Appendix D), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5 (no chunks). Disease groups are shown only as corpus distributions, with no results per task family or patient subgroup and no slice sizes; the single-turn intake includes demographics but no demographic slicing is reported.

quotes.text: These responses are simulated clinical observations, not measurements from real patients.

rationale: The paper states the case-specific findings are simulated, LLM-authored offline (generator model not named), and cases are clinician-authored. No governance for real data (IRB, DUA, de-identification) and no data terms separate from the Apache-2.0 code licence are stated.
